newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo firms warn of worsening business climate - poll.
newsitem.headline: Yugo firms warn of worsening business climate - poll.

text.p: Yugoslav businessmen warned of a deteriorating overall economic climate for companies and the possibility of further increases in prices, Belgrade-based Economics Institute said on Friday.
"The general economic climate in firms is bad, as are expectations," Goran Pitic, a prominent economist with the institute, told reporters on Friday.
According to a regular monthly poll conducted by the institute, 62.8 percent of the firms said the economic climate is bad and only 0.7 percent said it is good.
The Institute polled 300 Yugoslav firms covering 55 percent of all industry and 35 percent of total employed.
Despite a slowdown in monthly retail price growth in February to 0.6 percent against January, when prices rose 1.4 percent, inflationary expectations among firms were still high.
Prices remain a chronic problem, with 51.4 percent of the firms expecting input prices to go up and only 0.7 percent saying they will fall.
Around 27.4 percent expected prices of finished products to go up and 0.8 percent said they will fall.
These high percentages show the firms' uncertainty that the central bank will be able to maintain its restrictive monetary policy, said Miroljub Labus, another economist with the institute.
"If the (central) bank loosens its reigns, inflation will pick up very quickly," Labus said.
Since its peak in October last year, optimism among firms has been on the decline, with only 24.5 percent expecting improvement in the overall economy and 17.5 percent saying it will deteriorate.
Capacity utilisation in February was 57.2 percent, a slight decline from 57.7 percent utilisation in January.
Firms said the three main limiting factors to more dynamic production growth remain lack of credits (33.6 percent), low demand (25.3 percent) and shortage of raw materials (24.3).
Industrial output in February rose 11.4 percent against January when it dropped 20.8 percent on December.
About 43.2 percent of the firms do not plan to export goods in the next three months, which is a concern because of the high trade deficit, the report said.
Yugoslavia's trade deficit was $2.26 billion last year and stood at $351 million in the first two months this year.
